A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LittleBit work and contain 25 readable pages, including Appendices A-C. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable matching of equations, figures, tables and supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original LittleBit perplexity and zero-shot evaluations, ablations, generated samples, and measured kernel latency and decoding throughput in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original LittleBit perplexity and zero-shot results, ablations, generated samples, and kernel and decoding benchmarks, including Tables 13-14.

M1.justification: The factorized binary architecture, scaling vectors, Dual-SVID initialization, residual compensation, QAT losses and SmoothSign procedure are unchanged in Section 3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both retain WikiText-2, C4 and PTB evaluations, the same seven commonsense benchmarks, generation examples and inference benchmarks. Training data and evaluated model families also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: for example, Table 1 includes STBLLM, BiLLM, OneBit, BinaryMoS, GPTQ and OmniQuant, while Table 9 compares Wanda and SVD-LLMv2. Removed bibliography entries do not remove evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A.7-A.8 retain the same data usage, 2048-token sequences, five-epoch training, learning-rate settings, BPW/rank configurations and inference benchmark procedures.

E4.justification: The residual-compensation, SmoothSign-versus-STE and K/V-rank ablations in A.2 are unchanged. The pruning-versus-SVD analysis in A.5 and generation case studies in A.6 are also retained without revisions.

E5.justification: Table 14 states that decoding benchmarks were run ten times and averaged in both versions. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty or significance-reporting procedures are added, removed or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, plotted findings and generated samples are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 retains Llama2-7B perplexity of 10.47 at 0.55 BPW, and Table 14 retains 203.20 tokens/s for 128-token decoding at 0.1 BPW.

T1.justification: The forward-pass derivation and quantization-error propositions and proof sketches in A.1, BPW/rank derivations in A.4, and computational-cost analysis in A.8.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about extreme compression, methodological contributions, performance preservation, memory savings and potential kernel speedup. The added code sentence supplies access information rather than a new scientific claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of residual compensation, compression trade-offs, generation failures and inference efficiency are unchanged. Appendix B retains the language-model-head size bottleneck, QAT resource limitations and unresolved questions about capability retention.

D1.justification: v3 adds a LittleBit code-repository address, SamsungLabs/LittleBit, to the abstract; v2 provides no LittleBit code location. This adds concrete access guidance while implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography removes He et al. (2015), Glorot and Bengio (2010), and Hansen's AutoAWQ kernels (2024). Remaining works are matched across renumbering and reordering; the related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a code-availability sentence, alongside minor bibliographic editing and an updated arXiv version/date margin. Section order and substantive prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence causes limited first-page reflow, and bibliography removal/reordering changes the layout of pages 13-14. Figures, tables and appendix display structures are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer modestly improves reproducibility guidance by supplying a concrete code location absent from v2. Scientific evidence and limitations are retained, with only small bibliography and layout changes. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
